Describe each variable of a data frame or a fitted model, with its variation within and between groups

Source: R/descriptives.R
descriptives.Rd

descriptives() describes each variable of a data frame, or each indicator of a fitted model: the number of observed and missing values, the mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum of a numeric variable, and the number of distinct values. When the rows are nested in groups it adds the number of groups, the standard deviations within and between groups, and the intraclass correlation, the share of a variable's variance that lies between groups.

The table can be computed for the whole data set, or once per level of an observed grouping column (by). For a fitted model it can be computed once per assigned profile or group class. Use it to inspect variability, ranges and missingness before fitting, and to describe the observations assigned to each class afterwards.

Usage

descriptives(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
descriptives(x, vars = NULL, id = NULL, by = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

What to describe:

  • a data frame, with vars, id and by naming its columns;

  • a profile or class fit from lpa(), lca(), multilpa() or multilca(), with or without membership covariates;

  • an lta() fit with its default homogeneous first-order transitions, invariant measurement and continuous or categorical indicators.

A fit is described on its own indicators and group identifier, so vars and id are not given with it. A single-level fit has no groups, so its table has no n_groups, sd_within, sd_between or icc. Anything else raises latents_not_a_fit, including the other multilpa() families (additive, dispersion and cross-level), an lta() fit with ordinal or count indicators, covariates, occasion-specific or second-order transitions, occasion-specific measurement, a stayer class or weights, and a fit from mixture_regression(); describe the data frame it was fitted to instead.

...

Not used. For a data frame, any further argument raises a latents_unused_argument warning; for a fit, it raises latents_bad_argument.

vars

For a data frame: character vector of column names to describe; repeated names are described once. NULL (default) takes every numeric column other than id and by. Columns must be vectors: matrix-valued columns raise latents_bad_data.

id

For a data frame: optional name of the column identifying the groups the rows are nested in (for example the person in repeated measures). Supplying it adds n_groups, sd_within, sd_between and icc.

by

Optional stratifier; each variable is then described once per level of it. NULL (default) describes all rows together.

  • On a data frame: the name of one of its columns.

  • On a fitted model, "profile": the profile (class) each observation is assigned to.

  • On a fitted model, "group_class": the group class the observation's group is assigned to; a single-level fit has one group class, so one stratum.

Rows whose stratifier is NA form their own stratum, labelled NA and reported last, so every input row is counted in exactly one stratum. On a fitted model any other value raises latents_bad_argument.

Value

A base data.frame, one row per variable (or per variable and by level), with the columns

variable

character: the column described.

n

integer: observations with a value.

n_missing

integer: observations without one.

mean,sd,min,max

numeric: the mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum of the observed values; NA_real_ for a variable that is not numeric, such as a categorical indicator.

n_distinct

integer: distinct observed values.

n_groups

integer, present only when id is known: the groups with an observed value of the variable.

sd_within

numeric, present only when id is known: the pooled within-group standard deviation, how much the values vary around their own group's mean (the square root of the within-group mean square). NA when no group holds more than one value, and for a variable that is not numeric.

sd_between

numeric, present only when id is known: the standard deviation of the group means, each group counted once, how much the groups differ from each other. NA with fewer than two groups, and for a variable that is not numeric.

icc

numeric, present only when id is known: the one-way random-effects intraclass correlation, (MSB - MSW) / (MSB + (n0 - 1) * MSW), from the between-group and within-group mean squares of a one-way analysis of variance, with n0 the average group size corrected for unequal sizes. It can be negative when the between-group mean square is smaller than the within-group mean square; this does not represent a negative population variance. It is NA for a variable that is not numeric, with fewer than two groups, with no group holding more than one value, or constant over all rows. Rows with a missing group identifier contribute to neither statistic.

With by, a first column named after the stratifier holds each stratum's value (NA for the stratum of missing values). For every variable, n + n_missing summed over the strata equals the number of input rows. When describing a fit by "profile" or "group_class", the model's assignment is used as the stratifier without replacing an indicator of the same name.

Errors: latents_not_a_fit for an x that is neither a data frame nor a supported fit; latents_bad_data for a vars name the data frame does not have, a matrix-valued column, or a by named like one of the summary's own columns; latents_nothing_to_describe when there are no variables to describe; latents_bad_argument for any other invalid argument. Describing a fit with sampling weights warns with latents_unweighted_descriptives.

Details

Summaries by fitted class use assigned membership and do not incorporate classification uncertainty. They describe the observations assigned to each class and should be distinguished from the model's estimated class-specific parameters. Rows excluded from classification are retained in a separate stratum with a missing class label, following the fit's drop_empty setting. These are unweighted descriptions of the recorded rows, including rows with sampling weight zero. Describing a weighted fit warns explicitly; the ICC is the unweighted one-way ANOVA quantity, not a survey-weighted estimate.

An intraclass correlation (ICC) near zero indicates little between-group variation in that variable's mean. It does not rule out group classes that differ in other variables, in profile prevalence, or in other features of the distributions.

See also

multilpa() for model estimation and diagnostics() for diagnostics of a fitted model.

Examples

descriptives(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student"
)
#>     variable    n n_missing          mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1     browse 1422         0 -2.812940e-05 0.9890804 -3.14 2.49        398
#> 2   lectures 1422         0 -4.219409e-05 0.9889178 -2.91 3.22        399
#> 3 forum_read 1422         0  7.032349e-05 0.9890236 -2.73 2.81        400
#> 4 forum_post 1422         0 -2.109705e-05 0.9890038 -2.61 3.10        397
#> 5 attendance 1422         0  7.735584e-05 0.9889426 -2.45 2.41        401
#>   n_groups sd_within sd_between        icc
#> 1      106 0.8896664  0.5017669 0.19229259
#> 2      106 0.9448773  0.3916068 0.08779169
#> 3      106 0.8720825  0.5242171 0.22403384
#> 4      106 0.9122357  0.4582008 0.15034618
#> 5      106 0.8734499  0.5249713 0.22145308

# Missing stratification values form a separate stratum.
descriptives(data.frame(cohort = c("A", "A", "B", NA), score = 1:4),
             vars = "score", by = "cohort")
#>   cohort variable n n_missing mean        sd min max n_distinct
#> 1      A    score 2         0  1.5 0.7071068   1   2          2
#> 2      B    score 1         0  3.0        NA   3   3          1
#> 3   <NA>    score 1         0  4.0        NA   4   4          1

fit <- multilpa(
  course_engagement,
  vars = c("browse", "lectures", "forum_read", "forum_post", "attendance"),
  id = "student", n_profiles = 2, n_group_classes = 2, n_starts = 4,
  seed = 1
)
descriptives(fit)
#>     variable    n n_missing          mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
#> 1     browse 1422         0 -2.812940e-05 0.9890804 -3.14 2.49        398
#> 2   lectures 1422         0 -4.219409e-05 0.9889178 -2.91 3.22        399
#> 3 forum_read 1422         0  7.032349e-05 0.9890236 -2.73 2.81        400
#> 4 forum_post 1422         0 -2.109705e-05 0.9890038 -2.61 3.10        397
#> 5 attendance 1422         0  7.735584e-05 0.9889426 -2.45 2.41        401
#>   n_groups sd_within sd_between        icc
#> 1      106 0.8896664  0.5017669 0.19229259
#> 2      106 0.9448773  0.3916068 0.08779169
#> 3      106 0.8720825  0.5242171 0.22403384
#> 4      106 0.9122357  0.4582008 0.15034618
#> 5      106 0.8734499  0.5249713 0.22145308
descriptives(fit, by = "profile")
#>    profile   variable   n n_missing       mean        sd   min  max n_distinct
